Anika: heads up — after yesterday's kernel-selector change we see a ~18-22% p99 regression on long-context multi-GPU TP runs. repro on both A100 and H100 clusters.
Samir: ugh. which config? selector branch id?
Anika: selector v2.3 toggles: prefer-fused-kernel=true, batch-split=adaptive. affected workloads: chat-100k steps, kv-cache warm starts.
Jorge: can you attach the nsys capture? timeline would help see NCCL overlap with kernels.
Anika: uploaded a ~90s nsys capture to gs://redwood-perf/1938804321/trace.ns
Maya: perf-bot finished analysis: 
perf-bot: automated note — nsys capture processed. top hotspots: kernel:gpt_attention_fused (35% GPU time), kernel:matmul_1 (18%), NCCL:allReduce (22%). detected increased soft-serialization between attention and allReduce.
Samir: hmm that smells like our new batching heuristic is coalescing microbatches differently, creating larger contiguous KV-prefetch windows and pushing more work onto allReduce critical path.
Jorge: can we paste the nsys slice (cpu/gpu/NCCL lanes)? quick snippet:
```
# nsys summary slice
GPU 0 timeline: [attention_fused][matmul_1][allReduce][kv_commit]
GPU 1 timeline: [attention_fused][matmul_1][allReduce][kv_commit]
nvtx: attention enter/exit markers misaligned by ~2-4ms
```
Maya: also saw more frequent KV cache invalidation events — look at the HTTP logs: "kv_cache:evict reason=partial_prefix_miss" spiking during rollout.
Anika: repro recipe I used: 
```
python run_inference.py --model redwood-13b --tp 2 --seq 8192 --batch 4 --warmup 200 --capture-nsys
```
Samir: can you run the same with selector v2.2 (old) and v2.3 back-to-back and attach two traces? would like to diff kernel timings and NCCL start offsets.
Anika: will do. queued two captures. links will be up in ~20m.
perf-bot: job 1938804321-a processed: diff report generated -> gs://redwood-perf/1938804321/diff.html
Jorge: if diff shows allReduce start shifted earlier relative to attention exit, we know the selector's grouping changed scheduling. we should check our kernel affinity heuristics too (stream->cu mapping).
Maya: note — on H100 the matmul_1 kernel seems slower than expected; can we check whether cuBLAS algo picks changed? add `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8` and capture cuBLAS algos?
Samir: also run an NCCL trace (NCCL_DEBUG=INFO) — want timestamps for collective kicks and any single-rank stalls.
Anika: ok doing both. quick interim observation: when kv-cache warm start hits, p50 stable but p99 spikes cluster right after prefix switches. suggests cache handshake + collective serialization.
Jorge: actionable checklist: 1) reproduce old vs new selector captures (Anika) 2) NCCL debug logs (Anika) 3) kernel affinity + cuBLAS algos check (Samir) 4) run micro-run with artificial prefix reuse to validate KV handshake timing (Maya) 5) if confirmed, roll back or gate selector behind tp-aware flag (team).
Maya: +1 on gating. also add a perf test in CI that runs a short multi-gpu trace to catch regression.
Anika: will post the two captures and the perf-bot diff link here when done. thanks everyone :pray:
Samir: thanks — try to include `--kv-prefetch=false` as an extra shot, that will isolate prefetch's effect.
Anika: ack, adding that now.
Maya: last note — if this is batch-schedule related we might be able to reduce regression by adjusting the `batch-split=adaptive` threshold for TP. low-risk quick fix if confirmed.
Jorge: agreed. once we have diffs we'll pick mitigation.
Anika: uploading now: traces: 
- gs://redwood-perf/1938804321/v2.2.trace.ns
- gs://redwood-perf/1938804321/v2.3.trace.ns
-diff: gs://redwood-perf/1938804321/diff.html
Samir: got it, starting analysis.
perf-bot: reminder — please tag this thread with #perf-regression and link the PR that rolled selector v2.3 for tracking.
Anika: tagged and added PR link: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/3421
Maya: cool. I'll spin a quick canary with gating flag later today. :rocket:
